title: BEST Discovery Manifest
description: Schema for the /.well-known/best discovery manifest. Every BEST-compliant endpoint must expose this at GET /.well-known/best.

services.description: Service definitions with transport bindings. Keys are fully qualified service names (e.g. io.best.agents).

agents.description: Snapshot of the service descriptors this endpoint hosts (optional). This is a discovery hint, not a live directory — BEST defines no registry endpoint. Implementations that manage services dynamically may expose that as a domain (a list-services query and RegisterService command) under their own namespace. For dynamic systems this array may be omitted or contain only representative examples.

serviceDescriptor.description: The identity card for a BEST-compliant service — what it does, what commands it accepts, what events it produces. Declared in the manifest's agents array.

version.description: Semver version of the service implementation currently running (e.g. '1.2.0'). Allows consumers to know which version is live and supports gradual rollouts.

type.description: Service type classification (e.g. negotiation-service, pricing-engine, sensor).

endpoint.description: Base URL of this service's BEST surface. Consumers append /.well-known/best to discover transport bindings and send commands. Optional — omit if the service is not directly addressable.

accepts.description: CloudEvent type strings (PascalCase) identifying the command types this service ingests.

produces.description: CloudEvent type strings (PascalCase) identifying the event types this service publishes as a result of processing.

metadata.description: Opaque, service-defined key-value configuration. Intended for operational settings such as AI model name, system prompt, or provider credentials. The protocol does not interpret or validate the contents. Clients may read this field; the service owns and manages it.

service.description: A top-level service domain the runtime supports.

authentication.description: Authentication for this service alone. When present it governs every capability the service implements and the root block does not apply to them; when absent the root block applies. type 'none' declares a public surface: its capabilities are callable without a credential.

capability.description: A composable capability within a service.

name.description: Fully qualified capability name using reverse-domain notation. BEST built-in capabilities use the io.best.* prefix (e.g. io.best.agents.commands). Custom or domain-specific capabilities must use a unique reverse-domain prefix owned by the implementer (e.g. com.acme.trading, com.acme.inventory).

spec.description: URL to the capability specification. Required for io.best.* capabilities. Custom capabilities should host their own specification page and link it here when available.

schema.description: URL to the JSON Schema for this capability. Required for io.best.* capabilities. Custom capabilities should host their own schema and link it here when available.

service.description: Key of the service (in the manifest's services object) that implements this capability. Required when the capability name prefix does not match the service name — for example, when a custom service (com.acme.trading) implements a standard BEST capability (io.best.agents.commands). Consumers use this field to resolve which http.endpoint to call for the capability's endpoints. Omit only when the capability name shares its prefix with exactly one service key (e.g. io.best.agents.* capabilities under the io.best.agents service).

status.description: Capability availability status. 'active' means fully implemented. 'partial' means a subset of the capability's endpoints or features are implemented — consumers must not assume all required endpoints exist. 'planned' means not yet implemented. Omitted means active.

endpoints.description: Machine-readable list of HTTP endpoints exposed by this capability. Paths are relative to http.endpoint. The HTTP method signals whether each operation is a read (GET) or a write (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Consumers can use this to discover the catalogue URL, determine mutability, and self-bootstrap without reading the spec.

method.description: HTTP method. GET is read-only. POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE mutate state.

tenants.description: Multi-tenant manifest discovery. When present, signals that this is a multi-tenant host and provides a URI template for consumers to obtain a tenant-scoped manifest. The tenant manifest returned at the expanded URI is fully self-contained and must not include a tenants block of its own.

manifest.description: RFC 6570 URI template for tenant manifest discovery (e.g. https://api.example.com/.well-known/best/{tenantId}). {tenantId} is the only defined variable. Consumers expand this template with a known tenant ID to obtain a fully-resolved, self-contained manifest.

extensions.description: Vendor-defined static declarations that must ride in the manifest document itself. Keys should be reverse-domain identifiers owned by the declarer (e.g. com.acme.region); the io.best.* prefix remains reserved for the specification and must not be used by implementers. The core protocol never interprets the contents, validators check only that this is an object, and consumers must ignore extensions they do not understand. Extensions must never be required in order to use a core capability, and must never carry anything obtainable through ordinary capability surface (commands, queries, events, workflows) — anything dynamic, behavioral, or available after authentication belongs there instead. As part of the public manifest, contents are limited to information intended for unauthenticated disclosure.

pushChannels.description: Push channels this capability supports for delivering events to callers. All fields are optional — absence means the channel is not supported. Typically declared on the io.best.agents.events capability.

sse.description: Server-Sent Events stream supported at GET /events/stream — recommended for browser apps, CLI tools, and locally-running agents.

endpoint.description: Consumer-facing base URL for all HTTP operations. This must be the public or proxy-facing address reachable by consumers — never an internal backend address. All capability endpoint paths are appended to this URL.

authentication.description: Authentication requirements. At the manifest root it governs every service that declares none of its own; on a service entry it governs that service alone. Consumers must read it before calling anything else: a consumer that holds no credential registers through deviceAuthorizationUrl when it is present, and only when it is absent asks the person for a credential obtained out of band.

type.description: Authentication mechanism. Use 'none' for public endpoints.

scheme.description: For 'bearer': the Authorization header scheme (e.g. 'Bearer'). For 'apiKey': the header or query parameter name.

in.description: Where the API key is passed when type is 'apiKey'. Query placement should carry only short-lived exchanged tokens, never long-lived keys — see the security spec on token exchange and query-string credentials.

tokenUrl.description: An RFC 6749 token endpoint. Hosts serving header-constrained clients should accept the client_credentials grant and return a short-lived access token. Where deviceAuthorizationUrl is declared it also serves the RFC 8628 device-code grant that completes an agent registration, answering with access_token, token_type, expires_in when the credential is not durable, the BEST members name (the connection's name: the connection sent to deviceAuthorizationUrl, else the sign-in manifest's address), tenant_id and auth_header, and the credential block: note (required, beginning with the sign-in guidance's token text: $defs/signInGuidance), endpoint (required), and optionally manifest, ready_check, mcp (the connection as an MCP client's configuration, one entry keyed by name) and http (direct calls, with a placeholder for the credential). Every URL in the block the credential may be sent to is on the canonical endpoint host.

deviceAuthorizationUrl.description: How an agent obtains this credential by itself: an RFC 8628 device authorization endpoint. A form-encoded POST with client_id (caller-declared, never identity) and the optional BEST parameters connection (the connection's name: one word of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, made from the name the person gave the service, given back as the token answer's name), agent_label and credential_lifetime (durable | session) is answered at once with a service-generated device_code, a user_code, verification_uri, expires_in, interval and note (the sign-in guidance's device text, verbatim: $defs/signInGuidance). Requires tokenUrl and note. Omitted when credentials are only issued out of band.

docs.description: A page for people. A consumer never depends on it.

note.description: The sign-in guidance's manifest text, verbatim (SPEC.md, Sign-in Guidance): how the consumer signs the person in, keeps the credential out of the conversation and under the name the person gave the service. Required wherever deviceAuthorizationUrl is declared: the text of the version the manifest declares, or of a later one.

mcpAuthentication.description: Authentication requirements for connecting to an MCP server. Consumers (including AI agents and IDE tooling) must read this block and supply the declared credentials when connecting.

headers.description: Required HTTP headers for 'apiKey' type. Use when more than one header is needed (e.g. an API key and a tenant ID). For single-header API key auth, a one-entry array is preferred.

tokenUrl.description: Token endpoint URL for 'oauth2' or token-based flows.

mcpAuthHeader.description: Descriptor for a single required HTTP header when connecting to an MCP server.

description.description: Human-readable description of what value to supply.

example.description: Pre-filled example value. Tooling (e.g. VS Code Copilot MCP config generator) may use this to populate the header automatically. A per-tenant manifest may pre-fill this with the resolved tenant ID.

signInGuidance.description: The sign-in guidance (SPEC.md, Sign-in Guidance): what a consumer does at each step of signing a person in, in words a service that declares deviceAuthorizationUrl carries verbatim. One set per version that changed them, keyed by that version; the highest is current. manifest is that authentication block's note; device is the note of the device authorization answer; token begins the note of the token answer, and a service may add to it after. A service carries the texts of the version it declares, or of a later one.

manifest.const: For you, the agent, not the person: read this manifest with an HTTP request; never show it to them or open it in a browser. When the person asks you to sign them in, POST a form to deviceAuthorizationUrl with client_id set to your software's name, and give them the link it answers (verification_uri_complete, or verification_uri and user_code) to open in their own browser, where they sign in and approve you. Never open that link yourself or in a browser you control, never sign in for them, and never ask for a password. Then poll tokenUrl, no faster than interval. Its answer carries a secret credential: save it straight to your client's credential store or to a file only the person can read, and never put it in a message, a command or any output: read the rest of the answer without it.

device.const: Give the person this link, verification_uri_complete (or verification_uri and user_code), to open in their own browser, where they sign in and approve you. Never open it yourself or in a browser you control: approving is theirs. Then poll tokenUrl no faster than interval, with a form of grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code, device_code and client_id. Its answer carries a secret credential: save it straight to your client's credential store or to a file only the person can read, and never put it in a message, a command or any output: read the rest of the answer without it.

token.const: The credential is a secret. Keep it in your client's configuration or credential store and never repeat it in the conversation, in a message, a command or any output: read it from where you stored it. A transcript, commands and their output included, is not a secret store, and a credential that appears there is leaked and must be replaced. If your client cannot store it, say so instead of showing it.

manifest.const: For you, the agent, not the person: read this manifest with an HTTP request; never show it to them or open it in a browser. When the person asks you to sign them in, first name the connection: one word of lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, made from what they called this service (acme payroll dev becomes acme-payroll-dev; its host if they gave no name), and ask them to confirm it before you go on. Then POST a form to deviceAuthorizationUrl with client_id set to your software's name and connection set to that name, and give them the link it answers (verification_uri_complete, or verification_uri and user_code) to open in their own browser, where they sign in and approve you. Never open that link yourself or in a browser you control, never sign in for them, and never ask for a password. Then poll tokenUrl, no faster than interval. Its answer carries a secret credential and, in name, the connection's name: save the credential straight to your client's credential store or to a file only the person can read, under that name, and never put it in a message, a command or any output: read the rest of the answer without it.

token.const: The credential is a secret. Keep it in your client's configuration or credential store, under the name in this answer, the connection the person named: another name is another sign-in, kept apart, with its own credential and its own permissions. Never repeat it in the conversation, in a message, a command or any output: read it from where you stored it. A transcript, commands and their output included, is not a secret store, and a credential that appears there is leaked and must be replaced. If your client cannot store it, say so instead of showing it.
